title: One-level normalized singleton augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l and X a Noetherian scheme. Use O and its residue map q [def-sfb-internal-completion-section-transport]. Let a be a global section whose singleton generates kernelIdeal(q) on every slice [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators]. Let P be an actual integral K-flat complex [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and n a natural number. Let v be any chain map from complex(P) tensor the level-n dual singleton Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system] to the actual transported quotient complex at n [def-sfb-internal-quotient-tower-model]. Assume that composing its degree-zero tensor unit with v gives the prescribed quotient unit, and that v vanishes on each total-tensor summand whose Koszul degree is nonzero. Then v is a quasi-isomorphism. This assertion uses only one level: no transition compatibility, tower map, or inverse-limit equation is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Lemma derived-completion-koszul (0A0E), singleton augmentation; also proetale.tex, Section derived-completion-noetherian (099L) and Lemma naive-completion (099M).

proof.text: Choose the canonical principal reduction data. Its scalar is multiplication by the coefficient uniformizer. Apply the singleton coordinate comparison to identify the transported mapping cone with the dual Koszul tensor, preserving the unshifted unit and factoring the shifted inclusion through Koszul degree -1.

Use CoefficientCone.coneToTensor_zero and CoefficientCone.coneToTensor_quasiIso, the proved private finite-level helpers in CompletionTriangleComparison. Removing the equality transport from data.hobj gives a quasi-isomorphism c from the actual scalar mapping cone to the actual finite tensor quotient for every K-flat P.

Identify modules.mapHomologicalComplex.map(c) with e.hom followed by v, degree by degree. The mapped cone inclusions are jointly epic: map the cone identity decomposition through the additive modules functor. On the unshifted inclusion the two maps agree by hu and the normalized coordinate equation; on the shifted inclusion they are both zero by the cone desc formula and hz at bidegree (q+1,-1).
The exact additive modules functor preserves homology and quasi-isomorphisms. Thus e.hom followed by v is a quasi-isomorphism. Cancel the chain isomorphism e.hom to conclude QuasiIso v.

theorem koszul_finite_augmentation_quasiIso [IsNoetherian X]
    (a : ((ring l E X).obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections)
    (ha : ∀ U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} X,
      IsRingedIdealGeneratingList (ring l E X)
        (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).module
        (ConstantCompletion.kernelIdeal (residue l E X)).inclusion U 1
        (fun _ ↦ a.val (op U)))
    (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ)
    (hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) (.up ℤ)).kFlat P)
    (n : ℕ)
    (v : ((ringedKoszulTensorTower (ring l E X) 1 (fun _ ↦ a)).obj
        (complex l E X P)).obj (op n) ⟶ (quotients l E X P).obj (op n))
    (hu : ringedKoszulTensorUnitComponent (ring l E X) 1 (fun _ ↦ a)
        (complex l E X P) (op n) ≫ v = (quotientUnits l E X P).app (op n))
    (hz : ∀ p j : ℤ, j ≠ 0 →
      HomologicalComplex.ιMapBifunctor (complex l E X P)
          ((ringedKoszulDualTower (ring l E X) 1 (fun _ ↦ a)).obj (op n))
          (curriedTensor _) (.up ℤ) p j (p + j) rfl ≫ v.f (p + j) = 0) :
    QuasiIso v
